name: Cricket
facts: The first official Test match was played between Australia and England in Melbourne in 1877.
India won its first Cricket World Cup in 1983, beating the West Indies in the final at Lord's.
Sachin Tendulkar was the first player to score a double century in a men's One Day International, in 2010.
The Ashes is named after a mock obituary for English cricket published in 1882.
Don Bradman finished his Test career with a batting average of 99.94.
A cricket ball must weigh between 155.9 and 163 grams in men's cricket.
The first Twenty20 international was played between Australia and New Zealand in 2005.
India won the first ever T20 World Cup in 2007, beating Pakistan in the final.
The pitch is 22 yards long, the length of a 'chain', an old unit of measurement.
The first Cricket World Cup was held in England in 1975.
Jim Laker took 19 wickets in a single Test match against Australia in 1956.
Anil Kumble took all 10 wickets in a Test innings against Pakistan in 1999.
The first women's Cricket World Cup, in 1973, was held two years before the first men's.
Lord's Cricket Ground in London is often called the 'Home of Cricket'.
A 'duck' means getting out without scoring a run; the name comes from the shape of a duck's egg, like a zero.
The longest Test match, between South Africa and England in 1939, lasted 10 days and still ended in a draw.
The Indian Premier League began in 2008.
Muttiah Muralitharan is the leading wicket-taker in Test cricket, with 800 wickets.
Day-night Test matches use a pink ball, because it is easier to see under floodlights.
Umpires can agree to play without bails if the wind is so strong that it keeps blowing them off.
The Decision Review System (DRS) was first used in a Test match in 2008.
Kapil Dev scored 175 not out against Zimbabwe in the 1983 World Cup after India were 17 for 5.
A 'hat-trick' in cricket means taking wickets with three consecutive deliveries.
Mithali Raj was the first woman to score more than 7,000 runs in women's ODIs.
Brian Lara holds the record for the highest individual Test score: 400 not out against England in 2004.
